1	# Memory Loop Rollout Plan & Code Owner Questions
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	The memory loop is a subsystem that learns from session analytics and injects contextual guidance into future agent sessions. It currently exists as a **prototype** on the `agent-improvements` branch. This plan designs the rollout to external beta (opt-in) users and presents open storage/design questions for code owner feedback.
6	
7	**Current prototype state**: Core memory CRUD, generation, injection, outcome tracking, TUI dashboard, and lifecycle management all work but are stored in a single JSON file (`.entire/memory-loop.json`). The insights database (`.entire/insights.db`) is SQLite. The code needs restructuring for production use.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## 1. Storage Architecture Options
12	
13	The single biggest design decision. Currently memories live in a flat JSON file that's loaded/saved atomically. This won't scale.
14	
15	### Option A: SQLite-Only (Local)
16	
17	Migrate memories from JSON into a dedicated `.entire/memory-loop.db`.
18	
19	```
20	.entire/
21	  insights.db       <- session analytics (existing)
22	  memory-loop.db    <- memory records, injection logs, history (NEW)
23	```
24	
25	**Schema sketch:**
26	```sql
27	memories (id, kind, title, body, scope_kind, scope_value, status, origin,
28	          owner_id, fingerprint UNIQUE, confidence, strength, outcome,
29	          inject_count, match_count, created_at, updated_at,
30	          last_injected_at, last_matched_at)
31	memory_history (id, memory_id, type, at, detail, session_id)
32	injection_logs (id, session_id, prompt_preview, injected_at)
33	injection_log_memories (log_id, memory_id)
34	refresh_history (id, at, scope, generated_count, activated_count, ...)
35	```
36	
37	| Aspect | Assessment |
38	|--------|-----------|
39	| Personal memories | Fast indexed queries by `owner_id` |
40	| Repo memories | Local only -- not visible to other contributors |
41	| Branch memories | Easy cleanup: `DELETE WHERE scope_kind='branch' AND scope_value NOT IN (active branches)` |
42	| Session summaries | No change (already in insights.db) |
43	| Injection latency | Sub-millisecond indexed SELECT |
44	| Sharing | None |
45	| Durability | Lost if `.entire/` deleted or repo re-cloned |
46	
47	**Pros:** Simplest migration. Fastest local queries. No network dependency. WAL mode proven in insightsdb.
48	**Cons:** No sharing of repo memories across contributors. No backup beyond local filesystem. Memories lost on re-clone.
49	
50	---
51	
52	### Option B: SQLite Local + Checkpoint Branch Remote
53	
54	SQLite for all local reads/writes. Repo-scope active memories sync to `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch for sharing.
55	
56	```
57	Local:   .entire/memory-loop.db  <- all reads, all writes
58	           | sync on push/fetch
59	Remote:  entire/checkpoints/v1/memories/manifest.json  <- repo-active only
60	```
61	
62	**Sync model:**
63	- On `git push` or explicit `memory-loop sync`, repo-scope `active` memories serialized to checkpoint branch
64	- On `git fetch`/clone, manifest read and merged into local SQLite
65	- Personal and branch memories never leave local
66	- Conflict resolution: last-writer-wins per fingerprint; suppressed/archived state wins over candidate/active
67	
68	| Aspect | Assessment |
69	|--------|-----------|
70	| Personal memories | Local SQLite only, never synced |
71	| Repo memories | Local for speed, checkpoint branch for durability/sharing |
72	| Branch memories | Local only, pruned on branch delete |
73	| Injection latency | Sub-millisecond (reads from local SQLite) |
74	| Sharing | Repo-active memories shared via git push/fetch |
75	| Durability | Repo memories survive re-clone; personal do not |
76	
77	**Pros:** Fast local + durable remote. Uses existing checkpoint branch infrastructure (`WriteCommitted`/`ReadCommitted`). Clean personal/repo separation. Graceful offline.
78	**Cons:** Two sources of truth need reconciliation. Sync protocol adds complexity. Checkpoint branch format needs a `memories/` subtree.
79	
80	---
81	
82	### Option C: EntireDB-First
83	
84	All memories stored in EntireDB. Local cache only for offline fallback.
85	
86	EntireDB is our distributed git repository storage system with content-addressed immutable objects, DHT-based replication, and PostgreSQL for refs with CAS semantics. It already has checkpoint WebAPI endpoints (`GetExtendedCommit`, `ListExtendedCommits`).
87	
88	| Aspect | Assessment |
89	|--------|-----------|
90	| Personal memories | Stored in EntireDB under owner namespace |
91	| Repo memories | Globally visible via EntireDB |
92	| Injection latency | Network round-trip per TurnStart (10-200ms) |
93	| Sharing | Full sharing by default |
94	| Durability | Excellent: replicated, content-addressed, auditable |
95	
96	**Pros:** Single source of truth. Built-in replication and audit trail. No sync protocol.
97	**Cons:** Injection latency exceeds budget (lifecycle hook at `lifecycle.go:269` must return fast). Offline degradation. Personal memories stored remotely raises privacy concerns. Every command requires network.
98	
99	---
100	
101	### Option D: Git Branch Storage Only
102	
103	Store memories as JSON blobs on `entire/checkpoints/v1` alongside session metadata.
104	
105	```
106	entire/checkpoints/v1/
107	  memories/
108	    manifest.json
109	    <fingerprint[:2]>/<fingerprint[2:]>.json
110	  <checkpoint-id[:2]>/...   <- existing checkpoint data
111	```
112	
113	| Aspect | Assessment |
114	|--------|-----------|
115	| Personal memories | Not on branch (local JSON/SQLite only) |
116	| Repo memories | JSON blobs on checkpoint branch |
117	| Injection latency | Requires git object reads or local cache anyway |
118	| Sharing | Pushes with code |
119	
120	**Pros:** Infrastructure already exists. Git-native.
121	**Cons:** Not queryable without checkout. Injection hook would still need local cache for latency. Still need local storage for personal/branch memories. Effectively becomes Option B anyway.
122	
123	---
124	
125	### Comparison Matrix
126	
127	| | A: SQLite-only | B: SQLite + Remote | C: EntireDB-first | D: Git branch |
128	|---|---|---|---|---|
129	| Injection latency | <1ms | <1ms | 10-200ms | <1ms (cached) |
130	| Repo sharing | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
131	| Offline support | Full | Full | Degraded | Full |
132	| Implementation effort | Low | Medium | High | Medium |
133	| Migration from JSON | Simple | Simple + sync | Rewrite | Simple + sync |
134	| Personal privacy | Local | Local | Remote | Local |
135	
136	---
137	
138	## 2. Scope Mechanics
139	
140	### Personal (`me`)
141	- **Identity**: GitHub username via `githubidentity` package (already used, stored as `owner_id`)
142	- **Storage**: Local SQLite only
143	- **Activation**: Under `auto` policy -> active immediately. Under `review` -> stays candidate
144	- **Cross-repo portability**: Not in MVP. Future option: global `~/.entire/memory-loop.db`
145	
146	### Repo
147	- **Storage**: Local SQLite for reads. Optionally synced to checkpoint branch (Phase 2)
148	- **Governance**: Generated repo memories start as `candidate`. Require explicit `promote` to `active` (settled decision per HANDOFF doc)
149	- **Sharing**: Only `active` repo memories written to checkpoint branch. Candidates/suppressed/archived stay local
150	
151	### Branch
152	- **Storage**: Local SQLite only. Never synced
153	- **Cleanup**: Removed when branch no longer exists locally. Triggered on memory-loop entry points (`show`, `status`, `refresh`, `tui`)
154	- **Promotion**: Branch memories can be promoted to `me` or `repo` scope via TUI wizard
155	
156	### Cross-Scope Flow
157	```
158	Branch  --promote-->  Personal  --promote-->  Repo
159	                                                |
160	                                          (shared via
161	                                           checkpoint branch)
162	```
163	
164	---
165	
166	## 3. Performance & Size
167	
168	### Injection Latency Budget
169	
170	The hot path: `handleLifecycleTurnStart` -> `maybeInjectMemoryLoop` -> `LoadState` -> `PreviewSelection` -> format -> write response.
171	
172	**Current bottleneck**: JSON file parse is O(file size). With 200 records + history, file reaches 200-500KB.
173	
174	**With SQLite**: `SELECT * FROM memories WHERE status='active'` with index scan. Sub-millisecond for hundreds of records. `PreviewSelection` iterates only active records (typically 10-30).
175	
176	**Target**: <50ms total injection path. Log warning if exceeded.
177	
178	### Storage Caps
179	
180	| Scope | Realistic ceiling |
181	|-------|-------------------|
182	| Personal active | 20-50 |
183	| Repo active | 20-100 |
184	| Branch (per branch) | 5-20 |
185	| Total candidates | 50-200 |
186	| Total all statuses | Hard cap at 500 |
187	
188	### Session Summaries
189	Already in InsightsDB. No change needed. Add `VACUUM` after bulk prune deletes.
190	
191	### Loading Strategy
192	**Lazy**: Load only active records for injection (hot path). Full load for TUI/show/status (cold path).
193	
194	---
195	
196	## 4. Memory Quality & Generation
197	
198	### Current Scoring (`memoryloop.go:461`)
199	Token overlap (primary) + keyword phrase matching + outcome bonus (reinforced +2, ineffective -1) + scope bonus + cooldown penalty.
200	
201	### Improvements Needed
202	1. **Frequency weighting**: Records matched across more sessions score higher via `match_count`
203	2. **Recency weighting**: Recently updated memories get small bonus
204	3. **Diversity enforcement**: One memory per topic before taking a second
205	4. **Semantic similarity** (Phase 3): Embedding-based, not for MVP
206	
207	### Outcome Tracking
208	Current implementation: token-based comparison of pre/post injection sessions. This is noisy.
209	
210	**How it works today** (`memoryloop.go:1091-1138`):
211	1. Manual memories -> always neutral
212	2. Non-injected -> neutral
213	3. For injected memories: find sessions AFTER `LastInjectedAt`, check if problem tokens still appear
214	4. If problem tokens absent post-injection -> reinforced
215	5. If problem tokens still present -> ineffective
216	
217	**Improvements needed:**
218	- Track whether the *specific friction pattern* that generated a memory recurs post-injection (not just token overlap)
219	- Require 3+ injection cycles before marking ineffective (already the threshold)
220	- Use `PatternAnalysis.AffectedSessions` to check signal recurrence
221	
222	### Evidence Gate (already implemented in `generator.go:282`)
223	- Layer 1: Provenance via `source_signal` field
224	- Layer 2: `len(SourceSessionIDs) >= 2`
225	- Enforce at all thresholds, not just `strict`
226	
227	### Avoiding Generic Memories (already implemented)
228	- `genericAdvicePhrases` list, `generatedSpecificityMarkers`, `isGenericGeneratedCandidate` check
229	- Additional: require at least one specificity marker (file path, tool name, package name) in body
230	
231	---
232	
233	## 5. Manual Memory & Injection
234	
235	### Manual Add
236	`entire memory-loop add --kind <kind> --title <title> --body <body> [--scope me|repo]`
237	- Defaults to personal scope
238	- Manual memories active immediately (no candidate gate)
239	- Manual memories resist automatic pruning
240	
241	### Manual Mode Confirmation
242	When `mode=manual`, lifecycle hook writes a blocking prompt showing matched memories as suggestions. Agent sees them but they're framed as suggestions, not injected rules.
243	
244	### Coexistence
245	Manual and generated memories use the same `MemoryRecord` struct and selection pipeline. They compete equally on relevance score. Only difference: manual memories skip activation policy and auto-pruning.
246	
247	---
248	
249	## 6. Rollout Phases
250	
251	### Phase 1: MVP for External Beta
252	
253	**Goal**: Reliable local memory loop for a single developer per repo.
254	
255	**Scope:**
256	- Migrate JSON -> local SQLite (Option A)
257	- All three scopes (me, repo, branch) but repo is local-only
258	- Existing generation pipeline with evidence gate
259	- Existing injection with current scoring
260	- TUI dashboard
261	- Branch memory cleanup
262	- Prune command (time-based + ineffective-based)
263	- File materialization (apply to CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md)
264	- Mode `off|manual|auto`, policy `review|auto`
265	- Default: `mode=off` (opt-in)
266	
267	**Not in Phase 1:** No remote sync. No cross-contributor sharing. No cross-repo portability. No semantic scoring. No auto-refresh triggers.
268	
269	**Exit criteria:**
270	- 10+ beta users for 2+ weeks without data corruption
271	- Injection latency <50ms in instrumented builds
272	- No store exceeding 500 records without pruning
273	
274	### Phase 2: Shared Repo Memories
275	
276	**Goal**: Repo memories visible to all contributors.
277	
278	**Scope:**
279	- Sync repo-active memories to checkpoint branch (Option B)
280	- Read manifest on fetch/clone, merge into local SQLite
281	- Promotion workflow writes to checkpoint branch
282	- Conflict resolution (conservative merge)
283	- Owner provenance tracking
284	
285	**Exit criteria:**
286	- Two contributors see each other's promoted memories
287	- Merge conflicts resolved correctly
288	- No data loss on concurrent push
289	
290	### Phase 3: GA Readiness
291	
292	**Goal**: Production-quality, default-on for new repos.
293	
294	**Scope:**
295	- Cross-repo personal memory portability (`~/.entire/memory-loop.db`)
296	- Semantic scoring (embedding-based, optional)
297	- Auto-refresh triggers (after N sessions)
298	- Multi-contributor approval workflow
299	- Performance hardening
300	- User documentation
301	
302	---
303	
304	## 7. Code Owner Questions
305	
306	### 7.1 Storage
307	
308	**Q1: Which storage option for Phase 1?**
309	- (a) Option A: SQLite-only local -- simplest, no sharing
310	- (b) Option B: SQLite + checkpoint branch -- adds sharing from day one
311	- (c) Option D: Git branch -- reuses existing infra
312	- Recommended: **(a) for Phase 1, (b) for Phase 2**
313	
314	**Q2: Same database as InsightsDB or separate?**
315	- (a) Same `.entire/insights.db` -- simpler, one connection
316	- (b) Separate `.entire/memory-loop.db` -- cleaner separation
317	- Recommended: **(b) separate.** InsightsDB is a rebuildable cache. Memory state is user-created and not rebuildable. Different deletion semantics.
318	
319	**Q3: Hard cap on total memory records?**
320	- (a) 200  (b) 500  (c) 1000  (d) No cap
321	- Recommended: **(b) 500.** Each record ~1-3KB with history. 500 records ~ 1MB.
322	
323	**Q4: Migration strategy from JSON?**
324	- (a) Auto-migrate on first load, rename JSON to `.bak`
325	- (b) Explicit `entire memory-loop migrate` command
326	- (c) Parallel reads: try SQLite first, fall back to JSON
327	- Recommended: **(a) auto-migrate.** Transparent to users.
328	
329	---
330	
331	### 7.2 Scope & Sharing
332	
333	**Q5: Repo memories shared in beta, or local-only?**
334	- (a) Local-only for beta, sharing in Phase 2
335	- (b) Sharing from day one
336	- Recommended: **(a) local-only.** Sharing adds sync complexity.
337	
338	**Q6: When should branch memories be cleaned up?**
339	- (a) On entry points (show, status, refresh, tui) -- already designed
340	- (b) Also on `git branch -d` (post-checkout hook)
341	- (c) Only on explicit `prune`
342	- Recommended: **(a) entry points.** Non-invasive, already designed.
343	
344	**Q7: Personal memories portable across repos?**
345	- (a) No, repo-scoped only
346	- (b) Yes, via global `~/.entire/memory-loop.db`
347	- (c) Defer to Phase 3
348	- Recommended: **(c) defer.**
349	
350	**Q8: Can users adopt repo memories as personal (scope portability)?**
351	- (a) Yes, via TUI wizard
352	- (b) Yes, via CLI `memory-loop adopt <id> --scope me`
353	- (c) Not in MVP
354	- Recommended: **(a) TUI wizard.** Already designed in file materialization spec.
355	
356	**Q9: When promoting branch -> repo, what happens to the branch memory?**
357	- (a) Archive it (avoid duplicate injection)
358	- (b) Keep both
359	- (c) Delete it
360	- Recommended: **(a) archive.** Prevents double-injection.
361	
362	---
363	
364	### 7.3 Performance
365	
366	**Q10: Acceptable injection latency budget?**
367	- (a) 50ms  (b) 100ms  (c) 200ms
368	- Recommended: **(a) 50ms.** Hook is synchronous, delays agent start.
369	
370	**Q11: Instrumented latency logging?**
371	- (a) Always log when exceeding threshold (warn)
372	- (b) Only in debug mode
373	- Recommended: **(a) always.** Follows existing `perf.Start`/`perf.End` pattern in lifecycle.go.
374	
375	**Q12: Lazy vs eager loading?**
376	- (a) Lazy: `WHERE status='active'` for injection, full load for TUI
377	- (b) Eager: load all records always
378	- Recommended: **(a) lazy.** Primary performance benefit of SQLite migration.
379	
380	---
381	
382	### 7.4 Generation Quality
383	
384	**Q13: Default generation threshold for beta?**
385	- (a) `relaxed`  (b) `balanced`  (c) `strict`
386	- Recommended: **(b) balanced.**
387	
388	**Q14: Expose `relaxed` preset to external users?**
389	- (a) Yes, all three  (b) Only `balanced` and `strict` externally
390	- Recommended: **(b) hide relaxed.** Noisy generation undermines trust.
391	
392	**Q15: Enforce evidence gate at all thresholds?**
393	- (a) Yes, all thresholds  (b) Only at `strict`  (c) Provenance at balanced, both at strict
394	- Recommended: **(a) all thresholds.** Quiet system > noisy system.
395	
396	---
397	
398	### 7.5 Modes & Injection
399	
400	**Q16: Default mode for new repos?**
401	- (a) `off` -- explicit opt-in  (b) `manual` -- suggestions shown  (c) `auto` -- full injection
402	- Recommended: **(a) off for beta.** Switch to `manual` for GA.
403	
404	**Q17: Is `auto` activation policy available in beta?**
405	- (a) Both `review` and `auto`  (b) Only `review` in beta
406	- Recommended: **(a) both.** Useful for solo devs. Evidence gate filters weak candidates.
407	
408	**Q18: Max memories injected per turn?**
409	- (a) 2 (current)  (b) 3  (c) 5
410	- Recommended: **(a) keep at 2.** Less is more for prompt injection. Configurable via settings.
411	
412	---
413	
414	### 7.6 Lifecycle & Pruning
415	
416	**Q19: Should suppressed memories auto-archive eventually?**
417	- (a) Keep indefinitely (fingerprints block regeneration permanently)
418	- (b) Archive after 180 days
419	- (c) Archive after 90 days
420	- Recommended: **(a) indefinitely.** Suppression prevents re-generating rejected ideas.
421	
422	**Q20: Automatic lifecycle management for manual memories?**
423	- (a) Never auto-prune  (b) Auto-archive after 180 days no matches  (c) Warn in TUI, don't auto-prune
424	- Recommended: **(c) warn only.** Manual memories are explicit user intent.
425	
426	**Q21: Auto-trigger refresh, or manual only?**
427	- (a) Manual only (`entire memory-loop refresh`)
428	- (b) Auto after N sessions (configurable, default 5)
429	- (c) Auto on `git push`
430	- Recommended: **(a) manual for beta.** Add (b) in Phase 2.
431	
432	---
433	
434	### 7.7 UX
435	
436	**Q22: Memory-loop status in session banner?**
437	- (a) Show "N memories active" in banner  (b) Keep banner minimal  (c) Debug mode only
438	- Recommended: **(b) minimal.** Banner already multi-line.
439	
440	**Q23: TUI required for review, or CLI commands sufficient?**
441	- (a) CLI only  (b) TUI required  (c) Both
442	- Recommended: **(c) both.** CLI for scripting, TUI for interactive review.
443	
444	---
445	
446	## 8. Key Files
447	
448	| Component | Path | Notes |
449	|-----------|------|-------|
450	| Core store model | `cmd/entire/cli/memoryloop/memoryloop.go` | Must refactor for SQLite backend |
451	| Generator | `cmd/entire/cli/memoryloop/generator.go` | Stable for Phase 1 |
452	| Lifecycle injection | `cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go` | Hot path, must stay fast |
453	| CLI commands | `cmd/entire/cli/memory_loop_cmd.go` | 1743 lines, needs cleanup |
454	| InsightsDB (reference) | `cmd/entire/cli/insightsdb/db.go` | Pattern for SQLite WAL/migrations |
455	| Settings | `cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go` | MemoryLoopConfig struct |
456	| TUI | `cmd/entire/cli/memorylooptui/` | 4-tab dashboard |
457	| Checkpoint storage | `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/committed.go` | Phase 2 remote sync target |
458	| Handoff doc | `HANDOFF_MEMORY_LOOP.md` | Current status of prototype tasks |
459	
460	---
461	
462	## 9. Verification Plan
463	
464	Once the design is approved and implementation begins:
465	
466	1. **Unit tests**: `mise run test` -- all memory loop tests pass
467	2. **Integration tests**: `mise run test:integration` -- lifecycle injection tests
468	3. **SQLite migration**: Verify JSON -> SQLite migration preserves all records, history, and injection logs
469	4. **Injection latency**: Add timing instrumentation, verify <50ms
470	5. **Canary E2E**: `mise run test:e2e:canary` -- full pipeline works
471	6. **Manual QA**: Run `entire memory-loop refresh`, `show`, `status`, `tui` on a real repo with 20+ sessions
472

# Memory Loop Rollout Plan & Code Owner Questions

## Context

The memory loop is a subsystem that learns from session analytics and injects contextual guidance into future agent sessions. It currently exists as a **prototype** on the `agent-improvements` branch. This plan designs the rollout to external beta (opt-in) users and presents open storage/design questions for code owner feedback.

**Current prototype state**: Core memory CRUD, generation, injection, outcome tracking, TUI dashboard, and lifecycle management all work but are stored in a single JSON file (`.entire/memory-loop.json`). The insights database (`.entire/insights.db`) is SQLite. The code needs restructuring for production use.

---

## 1. Storage Architecture Options

The single biggest design decision. Currently memories live in a flat JSON file that's loaded/saved atomically. This won't scale.

### Option A: SQLite-Only (Local)

Migrate memories from JSON into a dedicated `.entire/memory-loop.db`.

```
.entire/
  insights.db       <- session analytics (existing)
  memory-loop.db    <- memory records, injection logs, history (NEW)
```

**Schema sketch:**
```sql
memories (id, kind, title, body, scope_kind, scope_value, status, origin,
          owner_id, fingerprint UNIQUE, confidence, strength, outcome,
          inject_count, match_count, created_at, updated_at,
          last_injected_at, last_matched_at)
memory_history (id, memory_id, type, at, detail, session_id)
injection_logs (id, session_id, prompt_preview, injected_at)
injection_log_memories (log_id, memory_id)
refresh_history (id, at, scope, generated_count, activated_count, ...)
```

| Aspect | Assessment |
|--------|-----------|
| Personal memories | Fast indexed queries by `owner_id` |
| Repo memories | Local only -- not visible to other contributors |
| Branch memories | Easy cleanup: `DELETE WHERE scope_kind='branch' AND scope_value NOT IN (active branches)` |
| Session summaries | No change (already in insights.db) |
| Injection latency | Sub-millisecond indexed SELECT |
| Sharing | None |
| Durability | Lost if `.entire/` deleted or repo re-cloned |

**Pros:** Simplest migration. Fastest local queries. No network dependency. WAL mode proven in insightsdb.
**Cons:** No sharing of repo memories across contributors. No backup beyond local filesystem. Memories lost on re-clone.

---

### Option B: SQLite Local + Checkpoint Branch Remote

SQLite for all local reads/writes. Repo-scope active memories sync to `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch for sharing.

```
Local:   .entire/memory-loop.db  <- all reads, all writes
           | sync on push/fetch
Remote:  entire/checkpoints/v1/memories/manifest.json  <- repo-active only
```

**Sync model:**
- On `git push` or explicit `memory-loop sync`, repo-scope `active` memories serialized to checkpoint branch
- On `git fetch`/clone, manifest read and merged into local SQLite
- Personal and branch memories never leave local
- Conflict resolution: last-writer-wins per fingerprint; suppressed/archived state wins over candidate/active

| Aspect | Assessment |
|--------|-----------|
| Personal memories | Local SQLite only, never synced |
| Repo memories | Local for speed, checkpoint branch for durability/sharing |
| Branch memories | Local only, pruned on branch delete |
| Injection latency | Sub-millisecond (reads from local SQLite) |
| Sharing | Repo-active memories shared via git push/fetch |
| Durability | Repo memories survive re-clone; personal do not |

**Pros:** Fast local + durable remote. Uses existing checkpoint branch infrastructure (`WriteCommitted`/`ReadCommitted`). Clean personal/repo separation. Graceful offline.
**Cons:** Two sources of truth need reconciliation. Sync protocol adds complexity. Checkpoint branch format needs a `memories/` subtree.

---

### Option C: EntireDB-First

All memories stored in EntireDB. Local cache only for offline fallback.

EntireDB is our distributed git repository storage system with content-addressed immutable objects, DHT-based replication, and PostgreSQL for refs with CAS semantics. It already has checkpoint WebAPI endpoints (`GetExtendedCommit`, `ListExtendedCommits`).

| Aspect | Assessment |
|--------|-----------|
| Personal memories | Stored in EntireDB under owner namespace |
| Repo memories | Globally visible via EntireDB |
| Injection latency | Network round-trip per TurnStart (10-200ms) |
| Sharing | Full sharing by default |
| Durability | Excellent: replicated, content-addressed, auditable |

**Pros:** Single source of truth. Built-in replication and audit trail. No sync protocol.
**Cons:** Injection latency exceeds budget (lifecycle hook at `lifecycle.go:269` must return fast). Offline degradation. Personal memories stored remotely raises privacy concerns. Every command requires network.

---

### Option D: Git Branch Storage Only

Store memories as JSON blobs on `entire/checkpoints/v1` alongside session metadata.

```
entire/checkpoints/v1/
  memories/
    manifest.json
    <fingerprint[:2]>/<fingerprint[2:]>.json
  <checkpoint-id[:2]>/...   <- existing checkpoint data
```

| Aspect | Assessment |
|--------|-----------|
| Personal memories | Not on branch (local JSON/SQLite only) |
| Repo memories | JSON blobs on checkpoint branch |
| Injection latency | Requires git object reads or local cache anyway |
| Sharing | Pushes with code |

**Pros:** Infrastructure already exists. Git-native.
**Cons:** Not queryable without checkout. Injection hook would still need local cache for latency. Still need local storage for personal/branch memories. Effectively becomes Option B anyway.

---

### Comparison Matrix

| | A: SQLite-only | B: SQLite + Remote | C: EntireDB-first | D: Git branch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Injection latency | <1ms | <1ms | 10-200ms | <1ms (cached) |
| Repo sharing | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Offline support | Full | Full | Degraded | Full |
| Implementation effort | Low | Medium | High | Medium |
| Migration from JSON | Simple | Simple + sync | Rewrite | Simple + sync |
| Personal privacy | Local | Local | Remote | Local |

---

## 2. Scope Mechanics

### Personal (`me`)
- **Identity**: GitHub username via `githubidentity` package (already used, stored as `owner_id`)
- **Storage**: Local SQLite only
- **Activation**: Under `auto` policy -> active immediately. Under `review` -> stays candidate
- **Cross-repo portability**: Not in MVP. Future option: global `~/.entire/memory-loop.db`

### Repo
- **Storage**: Local SQLite for reads. Optionally synced to checkpoint branch (Phase 2)
- **Governance**: Generated repo memories start as `candidate`. Require explicit `promote` to `active` (settled decision per HANDOFF doc)
- **Sharing**: Only `active` repo memories written to checkpoint branch. Candidates/suppressed/archived stay local

### Branch
- **Storage**: Local SQLite only. Never synced
- **Cleanup**: Removed when branch no longer exists locally. Triggered on memory-loop entry points (`show`, `status`, `refresh`, `tui`)
- **Promotion**: Branch memories can be promoted to `me` or `repo` scope via TUI wizard

### Cross-Scope Flow
```
Branch  --promote-->  Personal  --promote-->  Repo
                                                |
                                          (shared via
                                           checkpoint branch)
```

---

## 3. Performance & Size

### Injection Latency Budget

The hot path: `handleLifecycleTurnStart` -> `maybeInjectMemoryLoop` -> `LoadState` -> `PreviewSelection` -> format -> write response.

**Current bottleneck**: JSON file parse is O(file size). With 200 records + history, file reaches 200-500KB.

**With SQLite**: `SELECT * FROM memories WHERE status='active'` with index scan. Sub-millisecond for hundreds of records. `PreviewSelection` iterates only active records (typically 10-30).

**Target**: <50ms total injection path. Log warning if exceeded.

### Storage Caps

| Scope | Realistic ceiling |
|-------|-------------------|
| Personal active | 20-50 |
| Repo active | 20-100 |
| Branch (per branch) | 5-20 |
| Total candidates | 50-200 |
| Total all statuses | Hard cap at 500 |

### Session Summaries
Already in InsightsDB. No change needed. Add `VACUUM` after bulk prune deletes.

### Loading Strategy
**Lazy**: Load only active records for injection (hot path). Full load for TUI/show/status (cold path).

---

## 4. Memory Quality & Generation

### Current Scoring (`memoryloop.go:461`)
Token overlap (primary) + keyword phrase matching + outcome bonus (reinforced +2, ineffective -1) + scope bonus + cooldown penalty.

### Improvements Needed
1. **Frequency weighting**: Records matched across more sessions score higher via `match_count`
2. **Recency weighting**: Recently updated memories get small bonus
3. **Diversity enforcement**: One memory per topic before taking a second
4. **Semantic similarity** (Phase 3): Embedding-based, not for MVP

### Outcome Tracking
Current implementation: token-based comparison of pre/post injection sessions. This is noisy.

**How it works today** (`memoryloop.go:1091-1138`):
1. Manual memories -> always neutral
2. Non-injected -> neutral
3. For injected memories: find sessions AFTER `LastInjectedAt`, check if problem tokens still appear
4. If problem tokens absent post-injection -> reinforced
5. If problem tokens still present -> ineffective

**Improvements needed:**
- Track whether the *specific friction pattern* that generated a memory recurs post-injection (not just token overlap)
- Require 3+ injection cycles before marking ineffective (already the threshold)
- Use `PatternAnalysis.AffectedSessions` to check signal recurrence

### Evidence Gate (already implemented in `generator.go:282`)
- Layer 1: Provenance via `source_signal` field
- Layer 2: `len(SourceSessionIDs) >= 2`
- Enforce at all thresholds, not just `strict`

### Avoiding Generic Memories (already implemented)
- `genericAdvicePhrases` list, `generatedSpecificityMarkers`, `isGenericGeneratedCandidate` check
- Additional: require at least one specificity marker (file path, tool name, package name) in body

---

## 5. Manual Memory & Injection

### Manual Add
`entire memory-loop add --kind <kind> --title <title> --body <body> [--scope me|repo]`
- Defaults to personal scope
- Manual memories active immediately (no candidate gate)
- Manual memories resist automatic pruning

### Manual Mode Confirmation
When `mode=manual`, lifecycle hook writes a blocking prompt showing matched memories as suggestions. Agent sees them but they're framed as suggestions, not injected rules.

### Coexistence
Manual and generated memories use the same `MemoryRecord` struct and selection pipeline. They compete equally on relevance score. Only difference: manual memories skip activation policy and auto-pruning.

---

## 6. Rollout Phases

### Phase 1: MVP for External Beta

**Goal**: Reliable local memory loop for a single developer per repo.

**Scope:**
- Migrate JSON -> local SQLite (Option A)
- All three scopes (me, repo, branch) but repo is local-only
- Existing generation pipeline with evidence gate
- Existing injection with current scoring
- TUI dashboard
- Branch memory cleanup
- Prune command (time-based + ineffective-based)
- File materialization (apply to CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md)
- Mode `off|manual|auto`, policy `review|auto`
- Default: `mode=off` (opt-in)

**Not in Phase 1:** No remote sync. No cross-contributor sharing. No cross-repo portability. No semantic scoring. No auto-refresh triggers.

**Exit criteria:**
- 10+ beta users for 2+ weeks without data corruption
- Injection latency <50ms in instrumented builds
- No store exceeding 500 records without pruning

### Phase 2: Shared Repo Memories

**Goal**: Repo memories visible to all contributors.

**Scope:**
- Sync repo-active memories to checkpoint branch (Option B)
- Read manifest on fetch/clone, merge into local SQLite
- Promotion workflow writes to checkpoint branch
- Conflict resolution (conservative merge)
- Owner provenance tracking

**Exit criteria:**
- Two contributors see each other's promoted memories
- Merge conflicts resolved correctly
- No data loss on concurrent push

### Phase 3: GA Readiness

**Goal**: Production-quality, default-on for new repos.

**Scope:**
- Cross-repo personal memory portability (`~/.entire/memory-loop.db`)
- Semantic scoring (embedding-based, optional)
- Auto-refresh triggers (after N sessions)
- Multi-contributor approval workflow
- Performance hardening
- User documentation

---

## 7. Code Owner Questions

### 7.1 Storage

**Q1: Which storage option for Phase 1?**
- (a) Option A: SQLite-only local -- simplest, no sharing
- (b) Option B: SQLite + checkpoint branch -- adds sharing from day one
- (c) Option D: Git branch -- reuses existing infra
- Recommended: **(a) for Phase 1, (b) for Phase 2**

**Q2: Same database as InsightsDB or separate?**
- (a) Same `.entire/insights.db` -- simpler, one connection
- (b) Separate `.entire/memory-loop.db` -- cleaner separation
- Recommended: **(b) separate.** InsightsDB is a rebuildable cache. Memory state is user-created and not rebuildable. Different deletion semantics.

**Q3: Hard cap on total memory records?**
- (a) 200  (b) 500  (c) 1000  (d) No cap
- Recommended: **(b) 500.** Each record ~1-3KB with history. 500 records ~ 1MB.

**Q4: Migration strategy from JSON?**
- (a) Auto-migrate on first load, rename JSON to `.bak`
- (b) Explicit `entire memory-loop migrate` command
- (c) Parallel reads: try SQLite first, fall back to JSON
- Recommended: **(a) auto-migrate.** Transparent to users.

---

### 7.2 Scope & Sharing

**Q5: Repo memories shared in beta, or local-only?**
- (a) Local-only for beta, sharing in Phase 2
- (b) Sharing from day one
- Recommended: **(a) local-only.** Sharing adds sync complexity.

**Q6: When should branch memories be cleaned up?**
- (a) On entry points (show, status, refresh, tui) -- already designed
- (b) Also on `git branch -d` (post-checkout hook)
- (c) Only on explicit `prune`
- Recommended: **(a) entry points.** Non-invasive, already designed.

**Q7: Personal memories portable across repos?**
- (a) No, repo-scoped only
- (b) Yes, via global `~/.entire/memory-loop.db`
- (c) Defer to Phase 3
- Recommended: **(c) defer.**

**Q8: Can users adopt repo memories as personal (scope portability)?**
- (a) Yes, via TUI wizard
- (b) Yes, via CLI `memory-loop adopt <id> --scope me`
- (c) Not in MVP
- Recommended: **(a) TUI wizard.** Already designed in file materialization spec.

**Q9: When promoting branch -> repo, what happens to the branch memory?**
- (a) Archive it (avoid duplicate injection)
- (b) Keep both
- (c) Delete it
- Recommended: **(a) archive.** Prevents double-injection.

---

### 7.3 Performance

**Q10: Acceptable injection latency budget?**
- (a) 50ms  (b) 100ms  (c) 200ms
- Recommended: **(a) 50ms.** Hook is synchronous, delays agent start.

**Q11: Instrumented latency logging?**
- (a) Always log when exceeding threshold (warn)
- (b) Only in debug mode
- Recommended: **(a) always.** Follows existing `perf.Start`/`perf.End` pattern in lifecycle.go.

**Q12: Lazy vs eager loading?**
- (a) Lazy: `WHERE status='active'` for injection, full load for TUI
- (b) Eager: load all records always
- Recommended: **(a) lazy.** Primary performance benefit of SQLite migration.

---

### 7.4 Generation Quality

**Q13: Default generation threshold for beta?**
- (a) `relaxed`  (b) `balanced`  (c) `strict`
- Recommended: **(b) balanced.**

**Q14: Expose `relaxed` preset to external users?**
- (a) Yes, all three  (b) Only `balanced` and `strict` externally
- Recommended: **(b) hide relaxed.** Noisy generation undermines trust.

**Q15: Enforce evidence gate at all thresholds?**
- (a) Yes, all thresholds  (b) Only at `strict`  (c) Provenance at balanced, both at strict
- Recommended: **(a) all thresholds.** Quiet system > noisy system.

---

### 7.5 Modes & Injection

**Q16: Default mode for new repos?**
- (a) `off` -- explicit opt-in  (b) `manual` -- suggestions shown  (c) `auto` -- full injection
- Recommended: **(a) off for beta.** Switch to `manual` for GA.

**Q17: Is `auto` activation policy available in beta?**
- (a) Both `review` and `auto`  (b) Only `review` in beta
- Recommended: **(a) both.** Useful for solo devs. Evidence gate filters weak candidates.

**Q18: Max memories injected per turn?**
- (a) 2 (current)  (b) 3  (c) 5
- Recommended: **(a) keep at 2.** Less is more for prompt injection. Configurable via settings.

---

### 7.6 Lifecycle & Pruning

**Q19: Should suppressed memories auto-archive eventually?**
- (a) Keep indefinitely (fingerprints block regeneration permanently)
- (b) Archive after 180 days
- (c) Archive after 90 days
- Recommended: **(a) indefinitely.** Suppression prevents re-generating rejected ideas.

**Q20: Automatic lifecycle management for manual memories?**
- (a) Never auto-prune  (b) Auto-archive after 180 days no matches  (c) Warn in TUI, don't auto-prune
- Recommended: **(c) warn only.** Manual memories are explicit user intent.

**Q21: Auto-trigger refresh, or manual only?**
- (a) Manual only (`entire memory-loop refresh`)
- (b) Auto after N sessions (configurable, default 5)
- (c) Auto on `git push`
- Recommended: **(a) manual for beta.** Add (b) in Phase 2.

---

### 7.7 UX

**Q22: Memory-loop status in session banner?**
- (a) Show "N memories active" in banner  (b) Keep banner minimal  (c) Debug mode only
- Recommended: **(b) minimal.** Banner already multi-line.

**Q23: TUI required for review, or CLI commands sufficient?**
- (a) CLI only  (b) TUI required  (c) Both
- Recommended: **(c) both.** CLI for scripting, TUI for interactive review.

---

## 8. Key Files

| Component | Path | Notes |
|-----------|------|-------|
| Core store model | `cmd/entire/cli/memoryloop/memoryloop.go` | Must refactor for SQLite backend |
| Generator | `cmd/entire/cli/memoryloop/generator.go` | Stable for Phase 1 |
| Lifecycle injection | `cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go` | Hot path, must stay fast |
| CLI commands | `cmd/entire/cli/memory_loop_cmd.go` | 1743 lines, needs cleanup |
| InsightsDB (reference) | `cmd/entire/cli/insightsdb/db.go` | Pattern for SQLite WAL/migrations |
| Settings | `cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go` | MemoryLoopConfig struct |
| TUI | `cmd/entire/cli/memorylooptui/` | 4-tab dashboard |
| Checkpoint storage | `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/committed.go` | Phase 2 remote sync target |
| Handoff doc | `HANDOFF_MEMORY_LOOP.md` | Current status of prototype tasks |

---

## 9. Verification Plan

Once the design is approved and implementation begins:

1. **Unit tests**: `mise run test` -- all memory loop tests pass
2. **Integration tests**: `mise run test:integration` -- lifecycle injection tests
3. **SQLite migration**: Verify JSON -> SQLite migration preserves all records, history, and injection logs
4. **Injection latency**: Add timing instrumentation, verify <50ms
5. **Canary E2E**: `mise run test:e2e:canary` -- full pipeline works
6. **Manual QA**: Run `entire memory-loop refresh`, `show`, `status`, `tui` on a real repo with 20+ sessions

# Memory Loop Rollout Plan & Code Owner Questions

## Context

The memory loop is a subsystem that learns from session analytics and injects contextual guidance into future agent sessions. It currently exists as a **prototype** on the `agent-improvements` branch. This plan designs the rollout to external beta (opt-in) users and presents open storage/design questions for code owner feedback.

**Current prototype state**: Core memory CRUD, generation, injection, outcome tracking, TUI dashboard, and lifecycle management all work but are stored in a single JSON file (`.entire/memory-loop.json`). The insights database (`.entire/insights.db`) is SQLite. The code needs restructuring for production use.

---

## 1. Storage Architecture Options

The single biggest design decision. Currently memories live in a flat JSON file that's loaded/saved atomically. This won't scale.

### Option A: SQLite-Only (Local)

Migrate memories from JSON into a dedicated `.entire/memory-loop.db`.

```
.entire/
  insights.db       <- session analytics (existing)
  memory-loop.db    <- memory records, injection logs, history (NEW)
```

**Schema sketch:**
```sql
memories (id, kind, title, body, scope_kind, scope_value, status, origin,
          owner_id, fingerprint UNIQUE, confidence, strength, outcome,
          inject_count, match_count, created_at, updated_at,
          last_injected_at, last_matched_at)
memory_history (id, memory_id, type, at, detail, session_id)
injection_logs (id, session_id, prompt_preview, injected_at)
injection_log_memories (log_id, memory_id)
refresh_history (id, at, scope, generated_count, activated_count, ...)
```

| Aspect | Assessment |
|--------|-----------|
| Personal memories | Fast indexed queries by `owner_id` |
| Repo memories | Local only -- not visible to other contributors |
| Branch memories | Easy cleanup: `DELETE WHERE scope_kind='branch' AND scope_value NOT IN (active branches)` |
| Session summaries | No change (already in insights.db) |
| Injection latency | Sub-millisecond indexed SELECT |
| Sharing | None |
| Durability | Lost if `.entire/` deleted or repo re-cloned |

**Pros:** Simplest migration. Fastest local queries. No network dependency. WAL mode proven in insightsdb.
**Cons:** No sharing of repo memories across contributors. No backup beyond local filesystem. Memories lost on re-clone.

---

### Option B: SQLite Local + Checkpoint Branch Remote

SQLite for all local reads/writes. Repo-scope active memories sync to `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch for sharing.

```
Local:   .entire/memory-loop.db  <- all reads, all writes
           | sync on push/fetch
Remote:  entire/checkpoints/v1/memories/manifest.json  <- repo-active only
```

**Sync model:**
- On `git push` or explicit `memory-loop sync`, repo-scope `active` memories serialized to checkpoint branch
- On `git fetch`/clone, manifest read and merged into local SQLite
- Personal and branch memories never leave local
- Conflict resolution: last-writer-wins per fingerprint; suppressed/archived state wins over candidate/active

| Aspect | Assessment |
|--------|-----------|
| Personal memories | Local SQLite only, never synced |
| Repo memories | Local for speed, checkpoint branch for durability/sharing |
| Branch memories | Local only, pruned on branch delete |
| Injection latency | Sub-millisecond (reads from local SQLite) |
| Sharing | Repo-active memories shared via git push/fetch |
| Durability | Repo memories survive re-clone; personal do not |

**Pros:** Fast local + durable remote. Uses existing checkpoint branch infrastructure (`WriteCommitted`/`ReadCommitted`). Clean personal/repo separation. Graceful offline.
**Cons:** Two sources of truth need reconciliation. Sync protocol adds complexity. Checkpoint branch format needs a `memories/` subtree.

---

### Option C: EntireDB-First

All memories stored in EntireDB. Local cache only for offline fallback.

EntireDB is our distributed git repository storage system with content-addressed immutable objects, DHT-based replication, and PostgreSQL for refs with CAS semantics. It already has checkpoint WebAPI endpoints (`GetExtendedCommit`, `ListExtendedCommits`).

| Aspect | Assessment |
|--------|-----------|
| Personal memories | Stored in EntireDB under owner namespace |
| Repo memories | Globally visible via EntireDB |
| Injection latency | Network round-trip per TurnStart (10-200ms) |
| Sharing | Full sharing by default |
| Durability | Excellent: replicated, content-addressed, auditable |

**Pros:** Single source of truth. Built-in replication and audit trail. No sync protocol.
**Cons:** Injection latency exceeds budget (lifecycle hook at `lifecycle.go:269` must return fast). Offline degradation. Personal memories stored remotely raises privacy concerns. Every command requires network.

---

### Option D: Git Branch Storage Only

Store memories as JSON blobs on `entire/checkpoints/v1` alongside session metadata.

```
entire/checkpoints/v1/
  memories/
    manifest.json
    <fingerprint[:2]>/<fingerprint[2:]>.json
  <checkpoint-id[:2]>/...   <- existing checkpoint data
```

| Aspect | Assessment |
|--------|-----------|
| Personal memories | Not on branch (local JSON/SQLite only) |
| Repo memories | JSON blobs on checkpoint branch |
| Injection latency | Requires git object reads or local cache anyway |
| Sharing | Pushes with code |

**Pros:** Infrastructure already exists. Git-native.
**Cons:** Not queryable without checkout. Injection hook would still need local cache for latency. Still need local storage for personal/branch memories. Effectively becomes Option B anyway.

---

### Comparison Matrix

| | A: SQLite-only | B: SQLite + Remote | C: EntireDB-first | D: Git branch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Injection latency | <1ms | <1ms | 10-200ms | <1ms (cached) |
| Repo sharing | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Offline support | Full | Full | Degraded | Full |
| Implementation effort | Low | Medium | High | Medium |
| Migration from JSON | Simple | Simple + sync | Rewrite | Simple + sync |
| Personal privacy | Local | Local | Remote | Local |

---

## 2. Scope Mechanics

### Personal (`me`)
- **Identity**: GitHub username via `githubidentity` package (already used, stored as `owner_id`)
- **Storage**: Local SQLite only
- **Activation**: Under `auto` policy -> active immediately. Under `review` -> stays candidate
- **Cross-repo portability**: Not in MVP. Future option: global `~/.entire/memory-loop.db`

### Repo
- **Storage**: Local SQLite for reads. Optionally synced to checkpoint branch (Phase 2)
- **Governance**: Generated repo memories start as `candidate`. Require explicit `promote` to `active` (settled decision per HANDOFF doc)
- **Sharing**: Only `active` repo memories written to checkpoint branch. Candidates/suppressed/archived stay local

### Branch
- **Storage**: Local SQLite only. Never synced
- **Cleanup**: Removed when branch no longer exists locally. Triggered on memory-loop entry points (`show`, `status`, `refresh`, `tui`)
- **Promotion**: Branch memories can be promoted to `me` or `repo` scope via TUI wizard

### Cross-Scope Flow
```
Branch  --promote-->  Personal  --promote-->  Repo
                                                |
                                          (shared via
                                           checkpoint branch)
```

---

## 3. Performance & Size

### Injection Latency Budget

The hot path: `handleLifecycleTurnStart` -> `maybeInjectMemoryLoop` -> `LoadState` -> `PreviewSelection` -> format -> write response.

**Current bottleneck**: JSON file parse is O(file size). With 200 records + history, file reaches 200-500KB.

**With SQLite**: `SELECT * FROM memories WHERE status='active'` with index scan. Sub-millisecond for hundreds of records. `PreviewSelection` iterates only active records (typically 10-30).

**Target**: <50ms total injection path. Log warning if exceeded.

### Storage Caps

| Scope | Realistic ceiling |
|-------|-------------------|
| Personal active | 20-50 |
| Repo active | 20-100 |
| Branch (per branch) | 5-20 |
| Total candidates | 50-200 |
| Total all statuses | Hard cap at 500 |

### Session Summaries
Already in InsightsDB. No change needed. Add `VACUUM` after bulk prune deletes.

### Loading Strategy
**Lazy**: Load only active records for injection (hot path). Full load for TUI/show/status (cold path).

---

## 4. Memory Quality & Generation

### Current Scoring (`memoryloop.go:461`)
Token overlap (primary) + keyword phrase matching + outcome bonus (reinforced +2, ineffective -1) + scope bonus + cooldown penalty.

### Improvements Needed
1. **Frequency weighting**: Records matched across more sessions score higher via `match_count`
2. **Recency weighting**: Recently updated memories get small bonus
3. **Diversity enforcement**: One memory per topic before taking a second
4. **Semantic similarity** (Phase 3): Embedding-based, not for MVP

### Outcome Tracking
Current implementation: token-based comparison of pre/post injection sessions. This is noisy.

**How it works today** (`memoryloop.go:1091-1138`):
1. Manual memories -> always neutral
2. Non-injected -> neutral
3. For injected memories: find sessions AFTER `LastInjectedAt`, check if problem tokens still appear
4. If problem tokens absent post-injection -> reinforced
5. If problem tokens still present -> ineffective

**Improvements needed:**
- Track whether the *specific friction pattern* that generated a memory recurs post-injection (not just token overlap)
- Require 3+ injection cycles before marking ineffective (already the threshold)
- Use `PatternAnalysis.AffectedSessions` to check signal recurrence

### Evidence Gate (already implemented in `generator.go:282`)
- Layer 1: Provenance via `source_signal` field
- Layer 2: `len(SourceSessionIDs) >= 2`
- Enforce at all thresholds, not just `strict`

### Avoiding Generic Memories (already implemented)
- `genericAdvicePhrases` list, `generatedSpecificityMarkers`, `isGenericGeneratedCandidate` check
- Additional: require at least one specificity marker (file path, tool name, package name) in body

---

## 5. Manual Memory & Injection

### Manual Add
`entire memory-loop add --kind <kind> --title <title> --body <body> [--scope me|repo]`
- Defaults to personal scope
- Manual memories active immediately (no candidate gate)
- Manual memories resist automatic pruning

### Manual Mode Confirmation
When `mode=manual`, lifecycle hook writes a blocking prompt showing matched memories as suggestions. Agent sees them but they're framed as suggestions, not injected rules.

### Coexistence
Manual and generated memories use the same `MemoryRecord` struct and selection pipeline. They compete equally on relevance score. Only difference: manual memories skip activation policy and auto-pruning.

---

## 6. Rollout Phases

### Phase 1: MVP for External Beta

**Goal**: Reliable local memory loop for a single developer per repo.

**Scope:**
- Migrate JSON -> local SQLite (Option A)
- All three scopes (me, repo, branch) but repo is local-only
- Existing generation pipeline with evidence gate
- Existing injection with current scoring
- TUI dashboard
- Branch memory cleanup
- Prune command (time-based + ineffective-based)
- File materialization (apply to CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md)
- Mode `off|manual|auto`, policy `review|auto`
- Default: `mode=off` (opt-in)

**Not in Phase 1:** No remote sync. No cross-contributor sharing. No cross-repo portability. No semantic scoring. No auto-refresh triggers.

**Exit criteria:**
- 10+ beta users for 2+ weeks without data corruption
- Injection latency <50ms in instrumented builds
- No store exceeding 500 records without pruning

### Phase 2: Shared Repo Memories

**Goal**: Repo memories visible to all contributors.

**Scope:**
- Sync repo-active memories to checkpoint branch (Option B)
- Read manifest on fetch/clone, merge into local SQLite
- Promotion workflow writes to checkpoint branch
- Conflict resolution (conservative merge)
- Owner provenance tracking

**Exit criteria:**
- Two contributors see each other's promoted memories
- Merge conflicts resolved correctly
- No data loss on concurrent push

### Phase 3: GA Readiness

**Goal**: Production-quality, default-on for new repos.

**Scope:**
- Cross-repo personal memory portability (`~/.entire/memory-loop.db`)
- Semantic scoring (embedding-based, optional)
- Auto-refresh triggers (after N sessions)
- Multi-contributor approval workflow
- Performance hardening
- User documentation

---

## 7. Code Owner Questions

### 7.1 Storage

**Q1: Which storage option for Phase 1?**
- (a) Option A: SQLite-only local -- simplest, no sharing
- (b) Option B: SQLite + checkpoint branch -- adds sharing from day one
- (c) Option D: Git branch -- reuses existing infra
- Recommended: **(a) for Phase 1, (b) for Phase 2**

**Q2: Same database as InsightsDB or separate?**
- (a) Same `.entire/insights.db` -- simpler, one connection
- (b) Separate `.entire/memory-loop.db` -- cleaner separation
- Recommended: **(b) separate.** InsightsDB is a rebuildable cache. Memory state is user-created and not rebuildable. Different deletion semantics.

**Q3: Hard cap on total memory records?**
- (a) 200  (b) 500  (c) 1000  (d) No cap
- Recommended: **(b) 500.** Each record ~1-3KB with history. 500 records ~ 1MB.

**Q4: Migration strategy from JSON?**
- (a) Auto-migrate on first load, rename JSON to `.bak`
- (b) Explicit `entire memory-loop migrate` command
- (c) Parallel reads: try SQLite first, fall back to JSON
- Recommended: **(a) auto-migrate.** Transparent to users.

---

### 7.2 Scope & Sharing

**Q5: Repo memories shared in beta, or local-only?**
- (a) Local-only for beta, sharing in Phase 2
- (b) Sharing from day one
- Recommended: **(a) local-only.** Sharing adds sync complexity.

**Q6: When should branch memories be cleaned up?**
- (a) On entry points (show, status, refresh, tui) -- already designed
- (b) Also on `git branch -d` (post-checkout hook)
- (c) Only on explicit `prune`
- Recommended: **(a) entry points.** Non-invasive, already designed.

**Q7: Personal memories portable across repos?**
- (a) No, repo-scoped only
- (b) Yes, via global `~/.entire/memory-loop.db`
- (c) Defer to Phase 3
- Recommended: **(c) defer.**

**Q8: Can users adopt repo memories as personal (scope portability)?**
- (a) Yes, via TUI wizard
- (b) Yes, via CLI `memory-loop adopt <id> --scope me`
- (c) Not in MVP
- Recommended: **(a) TUI wizard.** Already designed in file materialization spec.

**Q9: When promoting branch -> repo, what happens to the branch memory?**
- (a) Archive it (avoid duplicate injection)
- (b) Keep both
- (c) Delete it
- Recommended: **(a) archive.** Prevents double-injection.

---

### 7.3 Performance

**Q10: Acceptable injection latency budget?**
- (a) 50ms  (b) 100ms  (c) 200ms
- Recommended: **(a) 50ms.** Hook is synchronous, delays agent start.

**Q11: Instrumented latency logging?**
- (a) Always log when exceeding threshold (warn)
- (b) Only in debug mode
- Recommended: **(a) always.** Follows existing `perf.Start`/`perf.End` pattern in lifecycle.go.

**Q12: Lazy vs eager loading?**
- (a) Lazy: `WHERE status='active'` for injection, full load for TUI
- (b) Eager: load all records always
- Recommended: **(a) lazy.** Primary performance benefit of SQLite migration.

---

### 7.4 Generation Quality

**Q13: Default generation threshold for beta?**
- (a) `relaxed`  (b) `balanced`  (c) `strict`
- Recommended: **(b) balanced.**

**Q14: Expose `relaxed` preset to external users?**
- (a) Yes, all three  (b) Only `balanced` and `strict` externally
- Recommended: **(b) hide relaxed.** Noisy generation undermines trust.

**Q15: Enforce evidence gate at all thresholds?**
- (a) Yes, all thresholds  (b) Only at `strict`  (c) Provenance at balanced, both at strict
- Recommended: **(a) all thresholds.** Quiet system > noisy system.

---

### 7.5 Modes & Injection

**Q16: Default mode for new repos?**
- (a) `off` -- explicit opt-in  (b) `manual` -- suggestions shown  (c) `auto` -- full injection
- Recommended: **(a) off for beta.** Switch to `manual` for GA.

**Q17: Is `auto` activation policy available in beta?**
- (a) Both `review` and `auto`  (b) Only `review` in beta
- Recommended: **(a) both.** Useful for solo devs. Evidence gate filters weak candidates.

**Q18: Max memories injected per turn?**
- (a) 2 (current)  (b) 3  (c) 5
- Recommended: **(a) keep at 2.** Less is more for prompt injection. Configurable via settings.

---

### 7.6 Lifecycle & Pruning

**Q19: Should suppressed memories auto-archive eventually?**
- (a) Keep indefinitely (fingerprints block regeneration permanently)
- (b) Archive after 180 days
- (c) Archive after 90 days
- Recommended: **(a) indefinitely.** Suppression prevents re-generating rejected ideas.

**Q20: Automatic lifecycle management for manual memories?**
- (a) Never auto-prune  (b) Auto-archive after 180 days no matches  (c) Warn in TUI, don't auto-prune
- Recommended: **(c) warn only.** Manual memories are explicit user intent.

**Q21: Auto-trigger refresh, or manual only?**
- (a) Manual only (`entire memory-loop refresh`)
- (b) Auto after N sessions (configurable, default 5)
- (c) Auto on `git push`
- Recommended: **(a) manual for beta.** Add (b) in Phase 2.

---

### 7.7 UX

**Q22: Memory-loop status in session banner?**
- (a) Show "N memories active" in banner  (b) Keep banner minimal  (c) Debug mode only
- Recommended: **(b) minimal.** Banner already multi-line.

**Q23: TUI required for review, or CLI commands sufficient?**
- (a) CLI only  (b) TUI required  (c) Both
- Recommended: **(c) both.** CLI for scripting, TUI for interactive review.

---

## 8. Key Files

| Component | Path | Notes |
|-----------|------|-------|
| Core store model | `cmd/entire/cli/memoryloop/memoryloop.go` | Must refactor for SQLite backend |
| Generator | `cmd/entire/cli/memoryloop/generator.go` | Stable for Phase 1 |
| Lifecycle injection | `cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go` | Hot path, must stay fast |
| CLI commands | `cmd/entire/cli/memory_loop_cmd.go` | 1743 lines, needs cleanup |
| InsightsDB (reference) | `cmd/entire/cli/insightsdb/db.go` | Pattern for SQLite WAL/migrations |
| Settings | `cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go` | MemoryLoopConfig struct |
| TUI | `cmd/entire/cli/memorylooptui/` | 4-tab dashboard |
| Checkpoint storage | `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/committed.go` | Phase 2 remote sync target |
| Handoff doc | `HANDOFF_MEMORY_LOOP.md` | Current status of prototype tasks |

---

## 9. Verification Plan

Once the design is approved and implementation begins:

1. **Unit tests**: `mise run test` -- all memory loop tests pass
2. **Integration tests**: `mise run test:integration` -- lifecycle injection tests
3. **SQLite migration**: Verify JSON -> SQLite migration preserves all records, history, and injection logs
4. **Injection latency**: Add timing instrumentation, verify <50ms
5. **Canary E2E**: `mise run test:e2e:canary` -- full pipeline works
6. **Manual QA**: Run `entire memory-loop refresh`, `show`, `status`, `tui` on a real repo with 20+ sessions

### Option C: SQLite Local Cache + EntireDB Remote

SQLite for all local reads/writes (same as Option B). EntireDB as the remote store instead of the checkpoint branch.

EntireDB is our distributed git repository storage system with content-addressed immutable objects, DHT-based replication, and PostgreSQL for refs with CAS semantics. It already has checkpoint WebAPI endpoints (`GetExtendedCommit`, `ListExtendedCommits`).

```
Local:   .entire/memory-loop.db  <- all reads, all writes
           | async sync via EntireDB API
Remote:  EntireDB checkpoint data  <- repo-active only
```

| Aspect | Assessment |
|--------|-----------|
| Personal memories | Local SQLite only (same as Option B) |
| Repo memories | Local for speed, EntireDB for durability/sharing |
| Injection latency | Sub-millisecond (reads from local SQLite, same as B) |
| Sharing | Repo-active memories shared via EntireDB API |
| Durability | Excellent: replicated, content-addressed, auditable |
| Offline support | Full (local SQLite always works, sync is async) |

**Pros:** Single remote source of truth. Built-in replication and audit trail. CAS semantics simplify conflict resolution compared to git branch merging. Same injection latency as Options A/B since reads are always local.
**Cons:** Adds EntireDB as a dependency for sharing (not needed for local-only use). Requires auth/network for sync operations. Personal memories stored remotely would raise privacy concerns (but this design keeps them local). Sync protocol is API-based rather than piggy-backing on git push/fetch.

**Key difference from Option B:** The sync target is EntireDB's API (CAS-based conflict resolution) vs the checkpoint git branch (git merge-based conflict resolution). The local read/write path is identical.
